FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 26 June 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and 
Agriculture Division Council. 

Pendimethalin EC is generally manufactured to contain 30 percent (m/m) of pendimethalin and 
used as a herbicide. 

In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the 
Insecticides Acid, 1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the 
restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded 
off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)*. The number 
of significant places retained in the rounded oflf value should be the same as that of the specified 
value in this standard.

Specification 



3.1 Pendimethalin technical employed in the 
manufacture of this material shall conform to 
IS 12685 : 1989. 

3.2 Physical 

3.2.1 Description 

The material shall be in the form for clear, 
homogenous and stable liquid. Sediment and/ 
or suspended matter shall be negligible. On 
dilution with water» it shall readily form an 
emulsion, suitable for spray. 

3.2«2 Cold Test 

No turbidity or separation of solid or oily matter 
shall occur when the material is subjected to the 
cold test at lO^'C as prescribed in 13.1 of 
IS 6940 : 1982 or at any other lower temperature 



as agreed to between the purchaser and the 
supplier. Introduction of a seeding crystal is 
tiot necessary for the test. 

3.2.3 Flash Point (Abel) 

When determined by the method prescribed in 
IS 1448 [ P : 20 ] : 1982, the flash point of the 
material shall be above 24'5'^C. 

3.2.4 Emulsion Stability 

Any separation including creaming at the tbj? 
and sedimentation at the bottom of 100 ml of 
emulsion prepared in standard hard water with 
2*0 ml of the EC, shall not exceed 2d ml when 
tested by the method prescHbed in T3*3 of 
IS 6940 : 1982. 

3.2.5 Heat Stability 

After treating in accordance with the method 
prescribed in 13.4 of IS 6940 : 1982 the material 
shall comply with the requirements specified in 
3.2.1 to 3.2.4 and 3.3.1. 

NOTE — The material need not be put to heat 
treatment, if it bas crossed half of its shelMife as 
declared on the container. 

3.3 Chemical 

3.3.1 Pendimethalin Content 

When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex B of IS 12685 : 1989. the observed pendi- 
methalin content, percent (m//?i), of any of the 
samples shall not differ from the declared 
nominal value by more than the percent tole- 
rance limits indicated below:

3.3.1.1 The actual value of pendimethalin con- 
tent in the formulations shall be calculated to 
the second decimal place and then rounded off 
to the first decimal place before applying the 
tolerances given in 3.3.1. 

3.3.1.2 The average pendimethalin content of 
all samples taken shall not be less than the 
declared nominal content.

3.4 Acidity/AIktlinity 

When tested by the method prescribed in 13.5.4 
of IS 6940: 1982 the acidity (as HtSOi ) or 
alkalinity ( as NaOH ) of the material stutll be 
not more than 0*5 percent by mass. 

4 PACKING 

The material shall be packed in mild steel or 
tinplate containers suitably and properly lac- 
quered from inside. In addition the material 
shall comply with the general packing require- 
ments given in 2 of IS 8190 ( Part 2 ) : 1988. 

5 MARKING 

The container shall bear legibly and indelibly 
the following information and any other in- 
formation as is necessary under the Insecticides 
Act, 1968 and Rules: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Name of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 



d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Net mass of contents; 

f) Nominal pendimethalin content, percent 
(m/m); and 

g) A cautionary notice worded as in Insecti- 
cides Act^ 1968 and Rules. 

6 SAMPLING 

Representative examples of the material shall be 
drawn as prescribed in IS 10627 : 1983. 

7 TESTS 

7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the appropriate 
methods referred to in 3.2, 3.3 and 3.4. 

7.2 Quality of Reagentt 

Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and 
distilled water ( see IS 1070 : 1977 ) shall be 
employed in tests. 

NOTE — *Pure cheinicals* shall mean chemicals 
that do not contain impurities which affect the 
resuhs of analysis. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act^ 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.

harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of 
goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
